newsitem.title: CANADA: Minera Rayrock says finds new Chile copper.
newsitem.headline: Minera Rayrock says finds new Chile copper.

text.p: Minera Rayrock Inc said on Wednesday it has found a new high grade oxidized copper orebody in Chile.
The orebody was intercepted by several drill holes including one that returned values arveraging 4.5 percent copper over 92 metres, the company said in a statement.
The company is calling the new orebody "Catalina." It was found in a previously untested area between the Zar Pit and the Zarina zone on the company's Ivan property.
The deposit was traced for 100 metres along a northwest-southeast strike, the company said.
It and remains open on strike and at depth.
"This discovery demonstrates that small but very significant orebodies may still be found on the Ivan property," said David Hutton, vice-president of Minera Rayrock.

The company's early estimate for the orebody is about 400,000 tonnes of 3.0 percent copper containing about 25 million pounds of copper. The ore is likely accessable through an expansion of the Zar pit or from the underground Ivan mine.
Minera said it expects the company's total production in 1997 to reach 24.6 million pounds of copper. About half of the anticipated production has been hedged at about US$1.00.
